The helper returns logical bytes and evidence buckets, performs no fetch or deletion, and leaves unknown facts as holds. A bucket never grants deletion permission. Recheck actual usage and ignored files before separately authorized removal.\\\\n\\\\nThe [bootstrap](scripts/bootstrap.ts), [manifest](scripts/package.json) and [lock](scripts/bun.lock) require exact commander 14.0.0, bun-types 1.3.14 and typescript 7.0.2 metadata before dependency-backed CLI execution. Bootstrap fails setup-required and never installs. Run helpers with Bun runtime auto-install disabled. Missing dependencies remain blocked. The isolated tested snapshot only supports that snapshot, not this caller, the current checkout or either host. [Helper setup](../../docs/testing/helper-setup.md) states the exact-copy validation boundary and retains historical setup evidence. It does not authorize installation or transfer a historical pass to this caller. Any future setup needs fresh authorization for an exact writable copy, registry, disabled lifecycle scripts and task-owned cache. Never install in an operative invocation or bypass bootstrap.\\\\n\\\\nDelivery reads [Opening a PR](playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) in full and retains its review, companion, commit, push, draft or ready authorization and actual-result gates. A local draft is not a created PR. An exposed built-in PR tool owns operations it covers, and a failed tool does not authorize a CLI bypass. Opening alone never starts Babysit. A read-only question stays in Investigation, with no PR; its specific exception takes precedence over the generic delivery route. Prototype and planning handoffs grant no implementation or external permission. Missing create-skill, deslop, matching controls or independent review remains an explicit blocked gate even when a reduced local artifact is useful.\\\\n\\\\n## Writing the reply\\\\n\\\\nWrite the reply clean as you draft it. A cleanup pass after drafting does not remove these patterns.\\\\n\\\\n- **Short declarative sentences.** One thought per sentence, ended with a period.\\\\n- **No long-dash character anywhere.** Write a file-list bullet as a sentence (\\\\\\\"`main.js` owns persistence and the IPC han…34401 tokens truncated… can see at a glance.\\\\n\\\\n- Do the first unit by hand to learn the recipe, then build the tool. Prove it by rerunning it on that unit and diffing against your hand-done version. Make the lever safe to rerun.\\\\n- Codemod or script for edits, generator for repetitive files, a dump-to-sqlite query for analysis, a rerunnable check for verification.\\\\n- A deterministic lever beats fan-out. If the tool can process every unit in one pass, run it yourself. Don't fan out delegates to hand-apply what a script can do.\\\\n- When you fan work out to subagents, write the lever as a skill they all read: the recipe, the verification contract, and the do-not-touch fences in one artifact. Keep it outside the delegates' write scope so they can't quietly edit the contract.\\\\n- Applying this principle produces a file. If you cited it and there is no codemod, script, generator, or delegate skill in the diff, you didn't apply it.\\\\n- Commit the lever when the work outlives the session.\\\\n\\\\n**Balance:** The bar is triviality, not repetition. A one-off still earns a lever when the lever is what makes the work checkable. Per the [Laziness Protocol](../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md), build the smallest script that does or proves the job, never a framework.\\\\n\\\\nDistinct from [Encode Lessons in Structure](../principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md), which makes a recurring instruction a durable guardrail. This is throughput and reviewability on the work in front of you. For scripting the verification itself, see [Prove It Works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Host capability and permission boundaries\\\\n\\\\nUse the [host capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to discover file reads, authorized writes, execution and persistence. A proposed tool is not a saved artifact. A saved artifact is not executed proof. Report the commands, exit status and comparisons you observed; if execution is denied or unavailable, state that proof is blocked and provide the proposed rerun and diff procedure as reduced capability. If source reads are unavailable, do not claim a verified recipe.\\\\n\\\\nDelegation requires user authorization and exposed independent-worker operations under the [orchestration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Keep the shared recipe outside worker write scopes. Sequential work is reduced capability and never proves independent workers. Preserve the [active workflow owner](../../references/workflow-ownership.md).\\\\n\\\\nRetaining the lever beyond the session does not grant commit permission. Commit only when authorized. Do not install dependencies, publish or perform external writes as incidental steps. Preserve `disable-model-invocation: true` metadata without assuming the host enforces it.\\\\n---\\\\nname: technical-writing\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\"Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages.\\\\\\\"\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Technical writing\\\\n\\\\nThe goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.\\\\n\\\\nThree rules sit above the layers:\\\\n\\\\n- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. \\\\\\\"In order to\\\\\\\" is \\\\\\\"to\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\"It is important to note that\\\\\\\" is nothing.\\\\n- **Use the short, everyday word.** \\\\\\\"Use\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"utilize\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\"Help\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"facilitate\\\\\\\". \\\\\\\"Do\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"perform\\\\\\\". A long word has to buy its length with precision.\\\\n- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.\\\\n\\\\nThe codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.\\\\n\\\\nDon't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: \\\\\\\"move\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"delete\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"a budget that only decreases\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"evacuate\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"ratchet\\\\\\\", or \\\\\\\"endgame\\\\\\\". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.\\\\n\\\\n## Vary the rhythm\\\\n\\\\nThe layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.\\\\n\\\\n- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.\\\\n- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.\\\\n- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.\\\\n- Be specific over sterile. Not \\\\\\\"schema changes can cause issues\\\\\\\" but \\\\\\\"a column rename fails the build\\\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)\\\\n\\\\nOne document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?\\\\n\\\\n- Action + learning: **tutorial**.\\\\n- Action + work: **how-to**.\\\\n- Understanding + work: **reference**.\\\\n- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.\\\\n\\\\nUse the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.\\\\n\\\\n**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will \\\\\\\"learn\\\\\\\". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as \\\\\\\"we\\\\\\\", in commands: \\\\\\\"First, do x. Now, do y.\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: \\\\\\\"If you want x, do y.\\\\\\\" Name the guide by the task: \\\\\\\"How to calibrate the radar array\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"Radar array calibration\\\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.\\\\n\\\\n**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit \\\\\\\"About...\\\\\\\" in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.\\\\n\\\\nDon't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.\\\\n\\\\n## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)\\\\n\\\\n- Talk to the reader as \\\\\\\"you\\\\\\\", in the present tense. \\\\\\\"Will\\\\\\\" only for things that genuinely happen later.\\\\n- Say who does what: \\\\\\\"the compiler checks\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"is checked\\\\\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.\\\\n- Write instructions as commands: \\\\\\\"Click Submit.\\\\\\\" State facts plainly. Never \\\\\\\"should be done\\\\\\\".\\\\n- Put the condition before the instruction: \\\\\\\"To delete the document, click Delete.\\\\\\\" The reader skips what does not apply.\\\\n- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.\\\\n- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no \\\\\\\"please\\\\\\\" in instructions, and never \\\\\\\"simply\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"easy\\\\\\\", or \\\\\\\"quickly\\\\\\\" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.\\\\n- Don't pre-announce (\\\\\\\"we will soon support...\\\\\\\") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.\\\\n- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never \\\\\\\"click here\\\\\\\". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.\\\\n- Headings carry the point, not just the topic (\\\\\\\"Pick the mode first\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"Modes\\\\\\\"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase (\\\\\\\"Create an instance\\\\\\\"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.\\\\n- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.\\\\n- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop \\\\\\\"etc.\\\\\\\" and say up front that a list is partial.\\\\n\\\\n## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)\\\\n\\\\n- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.\\\\n- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.\\\\n- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: \\\\\\\"If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur.\\\\\\\"\\\\n- Keep \\\\\\\"the\\\\\\\" and \\\\\\\"a\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Remove backup file\\\\\\\" reads two ways. \\\\\\\"Remove the backup file\\\\\\\" reads one.\\\\n- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If \\\\\\\"check\\\\\\\" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.\\\\n- Pick one word per action and stick to it: \\\\\\\"start\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"start\\\\\\\" here and \\\\\\\"initiate\\\\\\\" there.\\\\n- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: \\\\\\\"Install the component\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"the component must be installed\\\\\\\".\\\\n- Avoid \\\\\\\"-ing\\\\\\\" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.\\\\n\\\\n## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)\\\\n\\\\n- Keep words like \\\\\\\"only\\\\\\\" and \\\\\\\"not\\\\\\\" next to the word they change: \\\\\\\"only fails on growth\\\\\\\" and \\\\\\\"fails only on growth\\\\\\\" say different things.\\\\n- Break up long noun strings: \\\\\\\"the proto import budget check script\\\\\\\" becomes \\\\\\\"the script that checks the proto-import budget\\\\\\\".\\\\n- Make every \\\\\\\"it\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"they\\\\\\\", and \\\\\\\"this\\\\\\\" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use \\\\\\\"this\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"which\\\\\\\" to point at a whole clause.\\\\n- Don't drop verbs: \\\\\\\"Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime\\\\\\\" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.\\\\n- Keep the small words that show structure. \\\\\\\"Ensure that the switch is off\\\\\\\" keeps \\\\\\\"that\\\\\\\" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.\\\\n- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: \\\\\\\"the client and the host\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"the client and host\\\\\\\", when they are two things.\\\\n- Say which parts \\\\\\\"and\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"or\\\\\\\" joins when a sentence can group two ways. \\\\\\\"Both...and\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"either...or\\\\\\\", and \\\\\\\"if...then\\\\\\\" are free disambiguators.\\\\n- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.\\\\n- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with \\\\\\\"(s)\\\\\\\".\\\\n- No slashes: write \\\\\\\"a, b, or both\\\\\\\" instead of \\\\\\\"a/b\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"and/or\\\\\\\".\\\\n- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. A doc that says \\\\\\\"the gate\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"the ratchet\\\\\\\", and \\\\\\\"the budget check\\\\\\\" for one thing teaches three things. Rewording an unchanged sentence between edits costs the same way. Don't churn what didn't change.\\\\n- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors. A non-native reader, a translator, and an agent all parse plain constructions best.\\\\n\\\\n## Voice and repo specifics\\\\n\\\\n- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.\\\\n- PR descriptions and commit messages are writing too. Every layer except Diátaxis applies to them. A PR body is a briefing that a reviewer can read in under a minute. Do not paste swarm logs, SHA lists, or metric tables. Link them.\\\\n- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.\\\\n- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths and real symbols. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.\\\\n\\\\n## Worked example\\\\n\\\\nBefore:\\\\n\\\\n> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.\\\\n\\\\nAfter:\\\\n\\\\n> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.\\\\n\\\\n## Access and permissions\\\\n\\\\nUse the current session capabilities in `../../references/host-capabilities.md` to read documents and verify authorized edits. Supplied text is enough for a rewrite in the conversation. If document writes are unavailable or denied, return the proposed text and state that it was not saved. If the document cannot be read and no text was supplied, report the missing input. Do not invent its content. Read `../unslop/SKILL.md` before applying it. If that dependency is unavailable, report the gap and label the review partial. Preserve `disable-model-invocation` as source metadata; host enforcement needs observed evidence. These limits also apply to PR descriptions and commit messages.       "text": "# Synthetic invoice decision record\n\nDisplay contract: JavaScript Number.toFixed(2), including its binary floating-point rounding behavior. Capture observed outputs before edits for 0, 1.005, -1.005, 12.345, empty rows, NaN and Infinity.       "text": "let lastFormatted = '';\nfunction fixed(value) { return value.toFixed(2); }\nexport function formatInvoice(value) {\n  if (!Number.isFinite(value)) throw new Error('nonfinite');\n  lastFormatted = fixed(value);\n  return lastFormatted;\n}\nexport function formatRows(rows) { return rows.map(row => formatInvoice(row.total)); }\n// Separate known bug, outside formatter refactor: this sorts numeric strings lexically.\nexport function sortAmounts(values) { return values.toSorted(); }\n"

Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Technical writing\\n\\nThe goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.\\n\\nThree rules sit above the layers:\\n\\n- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. \\\"In order to\\\" is \\\"to\\\". \\\"It is important to note that\\\" is nothing.\\n- **Use the short, everyday word.** \\\"Use\\\", not \\\"utilize\\\". \\\"Help\\\", not \\\"facilitate\\\". \\\"Do\\\", not \\\"perform\\\". A long word has to buy its length with precision.\\n- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.\\n\\nThe codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.\\n\\nDon't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: \\\"move\\\", \\\"delete\\\", \\\"a budget that only decreases\\\", not \\\"evacuate\\\", \\\"ratchet\\\", or \\\"endgame\\\". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.\\n\\n## Vary the rhythm\\n\\nThe layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.\\n\\n- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.\\n- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.\\n- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.\\n- Be specific over sterile. Not \\\"schema changes can cause issues\\\" but \\\"a column rename fails the build\\\".\\n\\n## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)\\n\\nOne document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?\\n\\n- Action + learning: **tutorial**.\\n- Action + work: **how-to**.\\n- Understanding + work: **reference**.\\n- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.\\n\\nUse the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.\\n\\n**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will \\\"learn\\\". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as \\\"we\\\", in commands: \\\"First, do x. Now, do y.\\\"\\n\\n**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: \\\"If you want x, do y.\\\" Name the guide by the task: \\\"How to calibrate the radar array\\\", not \\\"Radar array calibration\\\".\\n\\n**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.\\n\\n**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit \\\"About...\\\" in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.\\n\\nDon't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.\\n\\n## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)\\n\\n- Talk to the reader as \\\"you\\\", in the present tense. \\\"Will\\\" only for things that genuinely happen later.\\n- Say who does what: \\\"the compiler checks\\\", not \\\"is checked\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.\\n- Write instructions as commands: \\\"Click Submit.\\\" State facts plainly. Never \\\"should be done\\\".\\n- Put the condition before the instruction: \\\"To delete the document, click Delete.\\\" The reader skips what does not apply.\\n- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.\\n- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no \\\"please\\\" in instructions, and never \\\"simply\\\", \\\"easy\\\", or \\\"quickly\\\" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.\\n- Don't pre-announce (\\\"we will soon support...\\\") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.\\n- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never \\\"click here\\\". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.\\n- Headings carry the point, not just the topic (\\\"Pick the mode first\\\", not \\\"Modes\\\"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase (\\\"Create an instance\\\"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.\\n- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.\\n- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop \\\"etc.\\\" and say up front that a list is partial.\\n\\n## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)\\n\\n- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.\\n- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.\\n- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: \\\"If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur.\\\"\\n- Keep \\\"the\\\" and \\\"a\\\": \\\"Remove backup file\\\" reads two ways. \\\"Remove the backup file\\\" reads one.\\n- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If \\\"check\\\" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.\\n- Pick one word per action and stick to it: \\\"start\\\", not \\\"start\\\" here and \\\"initiate\\\" there.\\n- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: \\\"Install the component\\\", not \\\"the component must be installed\\\".\\n- Avoid \\\"-ing\\\" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.\\n\\n## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)\\n\\n- Keep words like \\\"only\\\" and \\\"not\\\" next to the word they change: \\\"only fails on growth\\\" and \\\"fails only on growth\\\" say different things.\\n- Break up long noun strings: \\\"the proto import budget check script\\\" becomes \\\"the script that checks the proto-import budget\\\".\\n- Make every \\\"it\\\", \\\"they\\\", and \\\"this\\\" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use \\\"this\\\" or \\\"which\\\" to point at a whole clause.\\n- Don't drop verbs: \\\"Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime\\\" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.\\n- Keep the small words that show structure. \\\"Ensure that the switch is off\\\" keeps \\\"that\\\" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.\\n- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: \\\"the client and the host\\\", not \\\"the client and host\\\", when they are two things.\\n- Say which parts \\\"and\\\" or \\\"or\\\" joins when a sentence can group two ways. \\\"Both...and\\\", \\\"either...or\\\", and \\\"if...then\\\" are free disambiguators.\\n- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.\\n- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with \\\"(s)\\\".\\n- No slashes: write \\\"a, b, or both\\\" instead of \\\"a/b\\\" or \\\"and/or\\\".\\n- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. A doc that says \\\"the gate\\\", \\\"the ratchet\\\", and \\\"the budget check\\\" for one thing teaches three things. Rewording an unchanged sentence between edits costs the same way. Don't churn what didn't change.\\n- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors. A non-native reader, a translator, and an agent all parse plain constructions best.\\n\\n## Voice and repo specifics\\n\\n- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.\\n- PR descriptions and commit messages are writing too. Every layer except Diátaxis applies to them. A PR body is a briefing that a reviewer can read in under a minute. Do not paste swarm logs, SHA lists, or metric tables. Link them.\\n- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.\\n- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths and real symbols. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.\\n\\n## Worked example\\n\\nBefore:\\n\\n> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.\\n\\nAfter:\\n\\n> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.\\n\\n## Access and permissions\\n\\nUse the current session capabilities in `../../references/host-capabilities.md` to read documents and verify authorized edits. Supplied text is enough for a rewrite in the conversation. If document writes are unavailable or denied, return the proposed text and state that it was not saved. If the document cannot be read and no text was supplied, report the missing input. Do not invent its content. Read `../unslop/SKILL.md` before applying it. If that dependency is unavailable, report the gap and label the review partial. Preserve `disable-model-invocation` as source metadata; host enforcement needs observed evidence. These limits also apply to PR descriptions and commit messages. Sending, publishing, or creating external changes requires explicit authorization.\\n\"\n  }\n}"

      "text": "import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';\nimport { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { invoiceController } from '../working/invoice/controller.mjs';\nimport { inspectCachedTotal } from '../working/invoice/calculator.mjs';\nimport { exportAmounts } from '../working/invoice/exporter.mjs';\nimport { formatInvoice, formatRows, sortAmounts } from '../working/invoice/formatter.mjs';\nconst manifest=JSON.parse(readFileSync('outputs/working-manifest.json','utf8'));\nconst hashes=manifest.files.map(f=>({path:f.destination,observed:createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(f.destination)).digest('hex'),expected:f.sha256}));\nif(hashes.some(f=>f.observed!==f.expected)) throw Error('input hash mismatch');\nfunction observe(name,fn){try{return {name,status:'returned',value:fn()};}catch(e){return {name,status:'threw',message:e.message};}}\nconst observations=[\nobserve('controller rows qty 2 unitPrice 1.005',()=>invoiceController({rows:[{qty:2,unitPrice:1.005}]})),\nobserve('cache after controller',()=>inspectCachedTotal()),\nobserve('explicit bridge to exporter',()=>exportAmounts([invoiceController({rows:[{qty:2,unitPrice:1.005}]})])),\n...[0,1.005,-1.005,12.345,NaN,Infinity].map(n=>observe('formatInvoice '+String(n),()=>formatInvoice(n))),\nobserve('formatRows empty',()=>formatRows([])),\nobserve('exportAmounts empty',()=>exportAmounts([])),\nobserve('controller empty rows',()=>invoiceController({rows:[]})),\nobserve('controller NaN input',()=>String(invoiceController({rows:[{qty:1,unitPrice:NaN}]}).total)),\nobserve('sortAmounts strings',()=>sortAmounts(['2.00','10.00']))\n];\nconst report={hashes,observations};\nwriteFileSync('outputs/worker-aw-trace-01/probe-output.json',JSON.stringify(report,null,2)+'\\n');\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(report,null,2));\n"

      "text": "# Invoice total flow\n\n## Overview\n\nThe request-facing function computes a JavaScript number. Export converts supplied totals to strings with two decimal places. The supplied fixture has no HTTP route and no caller wiring the controller to the exporter. An end-to-end request-to-export integration cannot be confirmed from these files.\n\nAssignment `aw-trace-01`, predecessor `aw-bootstrap-01`, belongs to actual runtime identity `/root/aw_trace_01`. Task input and observed Git HEAD both equal `380fc527302a3c0cc2ba9d303492c5b0faddc678`. The frozen package source revision is separately supplied as `51f209daf83cd97d64f89881d66533bb59dc57db`. No package revision verification was performed.\n\n## Key concepts\n\n- The input invoice has `rows`, whose entries supply `qty` and `unitPrice`.\n- `calculate(rows)` returns the numeric sum and saves it in module state exposed through `inspectCachedTotal()`. See [calculator.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/calculator.mjs:1).\n- Export rows have a `total` property. They are not the quantity-and-price rows consumed by the calculator. See [formatter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/formatter.mjs:8).\n\n## How it works\n\n1. `invoiceController(invoice)` calls `invoiceFacade(invoice)` and wraps the returned number in `{ total }`. See [controller.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/controller.mjs:2).\n2. `invoiceFacade` passes the same invoice to `invoiceAdapter`. The adapter passes only `invoice.rows` to `calculate`. These wrappers add no validation or formatting. See [facade.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/facade.mjs:2) and [adapter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/adapter.mjs:2).\n3. `calculate` reduces the rows from zero, adding `row.qty * row.unitPrice`. It replaces `cachedTotal` and returns it. There is no tax, discount, currency handling, or rounding in this calculation. See [calculator.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/calculator.mjs:3).\n4. Separately, `exportAmounts(rows)` calls `formatRows(rows)`, then joins the resulting strings with newline characters. See [exporter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/exporter.mjs:2).\n5. `formatRows` sends each `row.total` to `formatInvoice`. The formatter rejects nonfinite numbers with `Error('nonfinite')`, calls the private `fixed` helper's `value.toFixed(2)`, stores the string in `lastFormatted`, and returns it. See [formatter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/formatter.mjs:2).\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  Invoice --> Controller[invoiceController]\n  Controller --> Facade[invoiceFacade]\n  Facade --> Adapter[invoiceAdapter]\n  Adapter --> Calculate[\"calculate(invoice.rows)\"]\n  Calculate --> Total[\"numeric total + cachedTotal\"]\n  Total --> Response[\"{ total }\"]\n  Response -. \"caller not supplied\" .-> ExportRows[\"rows with total\"]\n  ExportRows --> Export[exportAmounts]\n  Export --> Rows[formatRows]\n  Rows --> Format[\"formatInvoice → toFixed(2)\"]\n  Format --> Text[\"newline-separated text\"]\n```\n\nThe probe explicitly composed `exportAmounts([invoiceController(invoice)])` for an invoice with quantity 2 and unit price 1.005. It observed numeric total `2.01`, cache `2.01`, and exported string `\"2.01\"`. That composition is a demonstration in the probe, not discovered application wiring.\n\n## Where things live\n\n| File | Symbol and responsibility |\n| --- | --- |\n| [controller.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/controller.mjs:2) | `invoiceController` produces the numeric response. |\n| [facade.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/facade.mjs:2) | `invoiceFacade` forwards the invoice. |\n| [adapter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/adapter.mjs:2) | `invoiceAdapter` extracts calculation rows. |\n| [calculator.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/calculator.mjs:2) | `calculate` sums line amounts. |\n| [formatter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/formatter.mjs:3) | `formatInvoice` validates and formats totals. |\n| [exporter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/exporter.mjs:2) | `exportAmounts` joins formatted rows. |\n| [decision.md](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/decision.md:3) | Fixture contract for binary floating-point display behavior. |\n\n## Gotchas\n\n- Rounding happens after calculation, at the display boundary. The observed formatter outputs were `0 → \"0.00\"`, `1.005 → \"1.00\"`, `-1.005 → \"-1.00\"`, and `12.345 → \"12.35\"`. The fixture explicitly preserves JavaScript `toFixed(2)` behavior. See [decision.md](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/decision.md:3).\n- The controller does not invoke the formatter. A numeric NaN can leave the controller unchanged, as observed. The formatter rejects NaN and Infinity when an export or other caller invokes it. The decision note says formatter errors are not swallowed by the controller, but no controller-to-formatter call exists in the inspected code. See [controller.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/controller.mjs:2) and [decision.md](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/decision.md:5).\n- Empty calculation rows yield numeric zero. Empty formatter rows yield `[]`. Empty export rows yield `\"\"`. The probe observed each separately.\n- `cachedTotal` is shared module state and observable through `inspectCachedTotal`. Each completed calculation replaces it. `lastFormatted` is private module state with no reader in these files. See [calculator.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/calculator.mjs:1) and [formatter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/formatter.mjs:1).\n- `sortAmounts` uses default lexical sorting. The probe observed `[\"2.00\", \"10.00\"]` become `[\"10.00\", \"2.00\"]`. It is unrelated to the traced export path and is explicitly marked as a separate defect. See [formatter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/formatter.mjs:9).\n- There is no request schema validation in the supplied path. Multiplication and addition use ordinary JavaScript coercion. Neither export headers nor CSV escaping are implemented here, only newline joining. See [calculator.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/calculator.mjs:3) and [exporter.mjs](/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-013-20261016/reruns/local-02/absent-workers/outputs/working/invoice/exporter.mjs:2).\n\n## Evidence and limits\n\nThe saved Bun probe and its output verify all seven manifest hashes and record actual outputs. The source reads and command returns are retained in `operations.json` where captured. The first checklist-write and file-discovery operations remain in the tool transcript but are not duplicated there. One initial combined source read exceeded the display budget. The omitted middle was reread in smaller commands before tracing.\n\nProve It Works changed the verification choice to actual source readback, manifest hash comparison, and executed boundary probes. Build the Lever changed the proof into a saved rerunnable `probe.mjs`. The Unslop and technical-writing guidance shaped this explanation.\n\nThroughput checkpoint: n/a, read-only investigation. One assigned explainer traced the small fixture directly. Nested workers were forbidden and none were created. Requested model and effort were inherit-parent. Verify outputs; report terminal facts and limits without self-grading.\nRequested model/effort: inherit-parent. Observed model/effort: unknown.\n# Investigation\n\nYou own the answer. Preserve its Investigation routing for how, why, are-we-sure and choice-between-alternatives questions.\n\nBefore source reads or delegation, discover [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md) and follow [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use only exposed, authorized read operations. Inherit parent model and effort unless a supported explicit selection is observed. Requested models are not observed models. The routed skills own their prompt and source contracts; this playbook directly invokes no script helper.\n\n1. Route through the [how skill](../../how/SKILL.md). For motivation questions, also route through the [why skill](../../why/SKILL.md). Read their complete instructions and the prompts and source playbooks required by the chosen route. Keep every investigator and explainer read-only, including connector-backed reads. Inspect delegated findings before relying on them. If independent workers are unavailable or unauthorized, disclose reduced capability and apply the same roles sequentially. Name inaccessible, denied, failed and searched-empty sources separately. Limit the answer to inspected evidence. Missing required companions or no authorized relevant source reads blocks the dependent answer.\n2. Throughput checkpoint stays one line: `throughput checkpoint: n/a, read-only investigation`.\n3. Produce the how-shaped output, Overview / Key Concepts / How It Works / Where Things Live / Gotchas, omitting sections only as how permits. For a decision between alternatives, produce a recommendation with a tradeoffs table. For motivation, preserve why confidence tiers, source coverage, contradictions and unknowns within the investigation output. Cite actual inspected sources. Accessible sources that support the answer are enough to deliver it without starting a product build or prototype.\n4. Apply the [unslop skill](../../unslop/SKILL.md) to the reply.\n\nNo PR, no babysit, no [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) unless the investigation precedes a code change. If it does, hand back to the user and re-route to [Bug fix](bug-fix.md) or [Feature](feature.md). That handoff does not authorize implementation, commits, PR creation or other writes. The Investigation exception takes precedence over the mode index generic Opening a PR rule. Do not install tools, change credentials or modify source state to obtain evidence.\n\nReply with the investigation output. For are-we-sure answers, include your real judgment with reasons. Push back if the premise is wrong under the mode Autonomy rules. Broad autonomy never overrides user authorization or host permissions. Disclose unperformed reads, uncertain conclusions and reduced roles; structural checks establish no runtime behavior or independent-worker success.\n"

Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\n- **Foundational Thinking** (**principle-foundational-thinking**). Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.\\n- **Redesign from First Principles** (**principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.\\n- **Attack the Premise** (**principle-attack-the-premise**). Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.\\n- **Subtract Before You Add** (**principle-subtract-before-you-add**). Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.\\n- **Minimize Reader Load** (**principle-minimize-reader-load**). Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.\\n- **Outcome-Oriented Execution** (**principle-outcome-oriented-execution**). Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.\\n- **Experience First** (**principle-experience-first**). Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.\\n- **Exhaust the Design Space** (**principle-exhaust-the-design-space**). A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.\\n- **Build the Lever** (**principle-build-the-lever**). Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.\\n\\n**Architecture**\\n\\n- **Model the Domain** (**principle-model-the-domain**). Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.\\n- **Boundary Discipline** (**principle-boundary-discipline**). Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.\\n- **Type System Discipline** (**principle-type-system-discipline**). Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.\\n- **Make Operations Idempotent** (**principle-make-operations-idempotent**). Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.\\n- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs** (**principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis**). Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.\\n- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State** (**principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state**). Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.\\n\\n**Verification**\\n\\n- **Prove It Works** (**principle-prove-it-works**). After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or \\\"it compiles\\\".\\n- **Fix Root Causes** (**principle-fix-root-causes**). Debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause, reproduce first, ask why until you reach it.\\n- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.\\n- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation** (**principle-test-behavior-not-implementation**). Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns `undefined`, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.\\n- **Explain the Number** (**principle-explain-the-number**). Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.\\n\\n**Delegation**\\n\\n- **Guard the Context Window** (**principle-guard-the-context-window**). Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.\\n- **Never Block on the Human** (**principle-never-block-on-the-human**). Tempted to ask \\\"should I do X?\\\" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.\\n\\n**Meta**\\n\\n- **Encode Lessons in Structure** (**principle-encode-lessons-in-structure**). You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\\n\\n## Autonomy\\n\\n**Just do it within authorization.** Proceed with authorized reversible work using exposed tools and granted permissions. Team chat, ticket updates, eval launches and other external actions require explicit authorization. Upstream autonomy language grants no permission. Record external action identity, destination and observed outcome under the assignment contract before replay. Unknown outcomes block replay.\\n\\n**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.\\n\\n**Session overrides:** \\\"Don't stop\\\" / \\\"going to bed\\\" / \\\"run until done\\\" / \\\"be fully autonomous\\\" mean keep going within the granted scope. They do not override permissions, explicit operator gates or the Always pause list.\\n\\n**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say \\\"this doesn't earn its place\\\" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.\\n\\n## Subagents\\n\\nUse the [poteto role prompt](../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) for any independent worker you spawn inside a playbook step, including code-writing delegates and ad-hoc helpers. /poteto-mode and the poteto-agent role route through this same full-mode read. Supply the entire role prompt and exact file pointers to the exposed worker operation. Generic routing without that prompt and read skips the style contract. Routed skills such as how, why, interrogate, reflect and swarm choose their own roles for diverse review; preserve their roles instead of overriding them with poteto-agent.\\n\\nDefaults for every worker assignment follow the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use independent background execution only when exposed and observed. Do not claim it from a role name or flag. Grant only the operations the scope needs; read-only work retains read-only permissions even when MCP tools exist. Use file pointers rather than inlined bulk context. Record requested and observed model and effort separately under [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md).\\n\\nCode delegates tier by difficulty. Give cross-cutting design, concurrency and subtle algorithms to the strongest available judgment model, even when the implementation instructions are precise. Trivial mechanical edits use an available fast code model. Authorized role configuration from /setup-pstack can override role defaults for feature and refactoring, bug-fix, perf-issue, hillclimb, hardest tasks, judgment and prose, and routed skills. Select only supported models and efforts from current tool documentation or observed enumeration. A missing role line keeps the portable inherit-parent default. A role line of inherit-parent or auto omits explicit model selection. Unsupported configured models or efforts require a disclosed supported fallback, or blocked if that exact choice is required. The source-host named defaults are not portable availability evidence. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified.\\n\\nWithout an exposed and authorized independent-worker operation, apply the same full-mode and leaf reads sequentially only within authorized scope. Label reduced capability. Sequential roles are not independent workers, independent review, background execution or model diversity. If the playbook requires independence, leave that gate blocked rather than silently waiving it.\\n\\nA worker forbidden to spawn owns its assigned diff directly and returns it to the lead for review separation, as Feature step 4 requires. It never waits on a nested worker or replies \\\"standing by\\\". This exception does not waive the lead's required independent review. Before accepting any result, match assignment identity, exact input revision, full current head SHA, existing artifacts and observed method evidence. Reject stale results and missing artifacts under the assignment contract. Bookkeeping labels cannot satisfy these checks.\\n\\nYou own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Treat agreement as supporting evidence only after checking independence, the observed models and the underlying artifacts.\\n\\n**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. This holds for a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, and the next queue item. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a \\\"done\\\" summary.\\n\\n## Throughput checkpoint\\n\\nFor nontrivial multi-step work, write these four todo items before fan-out, as required by Feature step 3. Keep an inapplicable dimension with n/a and a reason. Rewrite the checkpoint at phase boundaries and return it with the evidence.\\n\\n- Blocking first steps. Gates run before fan-out.\\n- Independent workstreams. Disjoint files, services or layers parallelize. Shared writes serialize.\\n- Shared mutable state. Default to splitting the target using the separate-before-serializing-shared-state principle leaf. Serialize only for real invariants.\\n- Smallest safe decomposition. If one worker is best, name why.\\n\\nCode-coupled work goes to one owner with the checkpoint inline. That owner fans out after the blocking phase when authorized and supported. Parent-level fan-out is for independent artifacts. Assignment records and bookkeeping do not prove workers ran. Keep decision trails in an explicit owned local output path per show-me-your-work and its log helper contract. Missing helper setup or persistence stays visible; do not invent saved logs or cross-session continuity.\\n\\n## Integrated helper and delivery bindings\\n\\nRead the selected playbook's complete adapted helper and prompt contracts before dependent execution. The 23 bundled playbook routes below and the Bugbot rubric are local instructions. Historical task deferrals in those files are not proof of absence or permission to skip a present contract. Check the actual path. An absent required contract still blocks its dependent step.\\n\\n- Decision trails use [show-me-your-work](../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md), its [template](../show-me-your-work/references/decision-log-template.tsv) and [log helper](../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh).\\n\\n  Invoke the helper through authorized execution with exactly `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>`.\\n\\n  The nonempty logfile is an explicit owned local path.\\n\\n  Tabs, newlines and carriage returns are rejected before writes, and formula-leading cells are quoted.\\n\\n  Read back the trail and retain the skill's scoped transcript audit, cross-model review and Attention requirements.\\n\\n  Append-only logging proves neither unattended execution nor recovery.\\n- Multi-phase plans use [check-plan.mjs](scripts/check-plan.mjs) as `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/check-plan.mjs <plan.md>`.\\n\\n  It takes one positional path and reads without edits.\\n\\n  Exit 2 means usage or unreadable input, 1 means format problems, and 0 means structural success.\\n\\n  Keep capability declarations, live and perf evidence, independent review and exact-head receipts.\\n\\n  It checks pstack plans only.\\n\\n  It never validates another controller's plan, implementation or host behavior.\\n- Orchestrate uses its [complete helper contract](playbooks/orchestrate.md) and the real [CLI](scripts/orch/orch.ts) and [store](scripts/orch/store.ts).\\n\\n  Bind `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/orch/orch.ts --store <owned-store>` or explicit `ORCH_STORE` outside the package tree.\\n\\n  Use full JSON for standing orders and rows.\\n\\n  Preserve `inbox drain --peek --json` and actual drain receipts with durable readback before classification. `ledger check <pr> <full-head-sha>` returns NOT-VERIFIED and exit 2 for a missing key.\\n\\n  Usage or runtime errors exit 1.\\n\\n  Ledger rows replace the same key without enforcing verifier precedence.\\n\\n  The caller owns precedence, append-only attempt history, exact SHA syntax, artifact inspection, terminal states, permissions and current-head filtering.\\n\\n  The helper never spawns, waits or wakes workers.\\n\\n  Stale locks require ownership review, and `--force` requires explicit takeover permission even for a dead holder.\\n\\n  Frontier discovery uses local git and gt in the stack owner's clone and fails on unavailable metadata or pin mismatch.\\n\\n  Do not substitute this binding for the gt-free Autopilot stack workflow.\\n\\n  Atomic rename is not a crash-durability or adversarial-concurrency guarantee.\\n- Babysit and Shipping use the GitHub-specific read-only [watcher](scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr) through their complete playbooks.\\n\\n  From the package root bind `bun --no-install skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr` with explicit `--owner`, `--repo`, PR selection, `--head <number=full-40-character-head>` for every watched member, `--max-polls <remaining-count>` and `--timeout <remaining-seconds>`.\\n\\n  Freeze queued order with `--queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom-to-top-list>`.\\n\\n  Connected mode uses `--stack`, mutually exclusive with queued mode. `check` adds `--status-only`.\\n\\n  Inspect NDJSON schemaVersion 1 kind, terminal and reason.\\n\\n  Exit 0 includes status-only and proves no readiness by itself.\\n\\n  Codes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 64 identify conflicts, threads, checks, timeout, merge gates, query failures and usage.\\n\\n  A changed head, missing authentication or transport, or exhausted poll-budget blocks the result.\\n\\n  Queued WAITING with reason kind merge-queue is non-terminal.\\n\\n  Babysit reports the frontier merge-ready and stops that watcher.\\n\\n  Shipping waits for observed merge under its distinct rule.\\n\\n  Carry budgets across re-arms and retain an observed stop or deadline binding for a hard wall-clock limit.\\n\\n  The helper deadline is checked between polling work.\\n\\n  Do not add a second sleep loop or treat GitHub output as Origin evidence.\\n- Cleanup uses the [audit wrapper](scripts/worktree-audit.sh) and [implementation](scripts/worktree-audit.py) through its playbook with an explicit local `--repo` and verified `--base`, plus authorized `--history-map` and `--pr-state` exports when available. The helper returns logical bytes and evidence buckets, performs no fetch or deletion, and leaves unknown facts as holds. A bucket never grants deletion permission. Recheck actual usage and ignored files before separately authorized removal.\\n\\nThe [bootstrap](scripts/bootstrap.ts), [manifest](scripts/package.json) and [lock](scripts/bun.lock) require exact commander 14.0.0, bun-types 1.3.14 and typescript 7.0.2 metadata before dependency-backed CLI execution. Bootstrap fails setup-required and never installs. Run helpers with Bun runtime auto-install disabled. Missing dependencies remain blocked. The isolated tested snapshot only supports that snapshot, not this caller, the current checkout or either host. [Helper setup](../../docs/testing/helper-setup.md) states the exact-copy validation boundary and retains historical setup evidence. It does not authorize installation or transfer a historical pass to this caller. Any future setup needs fresh authorization for an exact writable copy, registry, disabled lifecycle scripts and task-owned cache. Never install in an operative invocation or bypass bootstrap.\\n\\nDelivery reads [Opening a PR](playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) in full and retains its review, companion, commit, push, draft or ready authorization and actual-result gates. A local draft is not a created PR. An exposed built-in PR tool owns operations it covers, and a failed tool does not authorize a CLI bypass. Opening alone never starts Babysit. A read-only question stays in Investigation, with no PR; its specific exception takes precedence over the generic delivery route. Prototype and planning handoffs grant no implementation or external permission. Missing create-skill, deslop, matching controls or independent review remains an explicit blocked gate even when a reduced local artifact is useful.\\n\\n## Writing the reply\\n\\nWrite the reply clean as you draft it. A cleanup pass after drafting does not remove these patterns.\\n\\n- **Short declarative sentences.** One thought per sentence, ended with a period.\\n- **No long-dash character anywhere.** Write a file-list bullet as a sentence (\\\"`main.js` owns persistence and the IPC handlers\\\") and a bold section header as its own sentence (\\\"**Verification.** End to end via CDP\\\").\\n- **A colon as a mid-sentence connector is also out** (unslop rule 14). A colon before a list is fine.\\n- **Terse is not an excuse to drop content.** Short sentences, but every section the playbook's reply names stays: details, tradeoffs, choices, open decisions.\\n- **Frame impact for the consumer and the maintainer.** Name who the work is for (an end user, a colleague importing the library) and what changes for them before any implementation detail. Then what the next engineer who owns this code inherits. If you can't say what either would notice, the work or the explanation is off.\\n- **Never fabricate a link, citation, or transcript reference.** Link only artifacts you produced or read this session.\\n- **Every claim carries its evidence or its label in the same sentence.** Measured, inferred, or guess. A prediction or an unseen cause is a guess. Never hand the human a check you could run.\\n\\nEvery playbook ends with a reply written this way. Link to the actual PR you read or created when authorized. Never claim a draft is a created PR. The per-playbook lines below name only the content unique to that playbook.\\n\\n## Comments\\n\\nComments follow the same rule as the reply. Write them clean as you go. Keep a comment only for a non-obvious *why* the code can't show. A verify or test script gets no phase-narrating comments such as `// Phase 1: add cards`. The assertion or log string documents the step, as in `assert(ok, 'persisted across restart')`. This applies to every file you produce, including the delegate's diff.\\n\\n## Playbooks\\n\\nOpen an available todo list, or an authorized local Markdown checklist if no todo operation exists. Record that reduced tool binding. Its first items are the matched playbook's steps, copied in verbatim, before any task-specific todos. A step you choose not to do stays in the list with a one-line `skip: <reason>`. Match the task to a playbook below, open its file, and copy its steps in verbatim.\\n\\nA large or cross-cutting effort (a migration across many call sites, an ambitious multi-part change), or work the user steps away from to trust later, routes to the **figure-it-out** skill even when a narrower playbook like Feature fits. Use **figure-it-out** whenever no bundled playbook fits. It designs a bespoke, rigorous playbook for the task. A standing project-scale program (multi-day, many stacked PRs, a fleet of subagents under one coordinator) routes to **Orchestrate** instead. figure-it-out designs one bespoke run, orchestrate runs the program.\\n\\n- **Investigation.** Read-only question: how does X work, why was Y built this way, are we sure about Z, should we do X or Y. `playbooks/investigation.md`.\\n- **Bug fix.** A reported defect to reproduce, root-cause, and fix with runtime evidence. `playbooks/bug-fix.md`.\\n- **Perf issue.** A measured slowness to trace and improve against a baseline. `playbooks/perf-issue.md`.\\n- **Hillclimb.** Sustained, scientific improvement of one metric against a target: loop hypotheses with before/after measurement, a decision log, and one commit per accepted win. Distinct from Perf issue, which is a one-off fix. `playbooks/hillclimb.md`.\\n- **Runtime forensics.** Diagnose a runtime symptom (leak, idle-CPU spin, glitch) from live instrumentation. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix. `playbooks/runtime-forensics.md`.\\n- **Trace forensics.** Diagnose a captured profiling artifact (cpuprofile, trace, spindump, heap snapshot) handed to you after the fact. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix. `playbooks/trace-forensics.md`.\\n- **Feature.** New or changed behavior, built from a named data shape. `playbooks/feature.md`.\\n- **Refactoring.** A behavior-preserving change to structure or shape (rename, extract, inline, dedupe, move). `playbooks/refactoring.md`.\\n- **Prototype.** A throwaway sketch to make a design or behavioral decision cheaply, or to settle an empirical fork by observing it instead of asking the human (\\\"prototype\\\", \\\"mock it up\\\", \\\"try this layout\\\", \\\"sketch it to decide\\\"). `playbooks/prototype.md`.\\n- **Visual parity.** Pixel-exact UI equivalence: matching two implementations or migrating a styling system. `playbooks/visual-parity.md`.\\n- **Authoring or modifying a skill.** Writing or editing a SKILL.md. `playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md`.\\n- **Eval.** Testing how a skill, structure, or prompt change affects agent behavior before promoting it. `playbooks/eval.md`.\\n- **Babysit.** Driving a PR or a stack to merge-ready: conflicts, review threads, CI. `playbooks/babysit.md`.\\n- **Shipping.** The half after Babysit. Independently verifying a green stack, then landing the contiguous verified run bottom-up through `gh` by default or Origin when its CLI is available. `playbooks/shipping.md`.\\n- **Autonomous run.** A long task to drive to completion without stopping (\\\"run until done\\\", \\\"/loop until X\\\"). `playbooks/autonomous-run.md`.\\n- **Orchestrate.** A standing project handed to one coordinator chat: multi-day, many stacked PRs, dozens to hundreds of subagents, minimal human turns (\\\"run this whole project\\\", \\\"own this migration until it lands\\\"). Distinct from Autonomous run, which drives one task to a predicate. Work one agent could finish inside the session's budget routes there, not here, however program-shaped the phrasing sounds. `playbooks/orchestrate.md`.\\n- **Autopilot-full.** A queue of independent PRs run to merged with full autonomy. One owner per PR carries build through merge, and the root swarm-verifies each PR before its owner merges (\\\"autopilot this queue\\\", \\\"full autopilot\\\", one-owner-per-PR programs). `playbooks/autopilot-full.md`.\\n- **Autopilot-stack.** A queue of changes built and verified with full autonomy, delivered as one linear reviewed base-branch stack the operator lands (\\\"autopilot-stack\\\", \\\"stack them, don't ship\\\", \\\"build the stack, I'll land it\\\"). `playbooks/autopilot-stack.md`.\\n- **Session pickup.** Resuming or taking over a prior agent's in-flight work from a transcript, cloud-agent URL, or pushed branch. `playbooks/session-pickup.md`.\\n- **Pause safely.** Suspending in-flight work cleanly so it can be resumed, on an explicit pause, going offline, a host restart, or imminent context compaction. The complement to Session pickup. Full steps: `playbooks/pause-safely.md`.\\n- **Multi-phase or multi-PR plan.** Work that spans phases or stacked PRs. `playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md`.\\n- **Worktree and simulator cleanup.** Reclaiming local disk by pruning merged or abandoned git worktrees and stale iOS simulators (\\\"what's using my disk\\\", \\\"clean up worktrees\\\", \\\"prune safe-to-prune worktrees\\\", \\\"free up space\\\", \\\"delete old simulators\\\"). `playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md`.\\n- **Opening a PR.** Invoked at the end of every other playbook. `playbooks/opening-a-pr.md`.\\n### Orchestrate\\n\\nRead [poteto-mode](../SKILL.md), [capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md), [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), and the [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) in full. This playbook responds to \\\"run this whole project\\\" and \\\"own this migration until it lands\\\". Aliases do not register host commands. Read applied principles and routed skills before dependent work. Use [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md), [figure-it-out](../../figure-it-out/SKILL.md), [show-me-your-work](../../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md), [separate shared state](../../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md), and [encode lessons](../../principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md) where the steps call for them. Apply [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md) to briefs and reports.\\n\\nA program needs observed independent worker operations, isolated ownership, execution, persistence and result inspection. Without workers, authorized sequential work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy a required independent review or standing program. Without execution or writable persistence, block helper-dependent work and offer a scoped read-only handoff. Missing wake or remote placement means foreground operation only. Recurring wakes need explicit scheduling authorization. No unattended continuity is implied. Commits, pushes, PR creation, merges, messages, deployments, deletion and setup each retain their applicable permission gates. Gate defaults never grant permission by silence.\\n\\nThe companion wake mechanism is a host capability, not a bundled loop skill. Pending caller paths are `playbooks/autonomous-run.md` and `playbooks/babysit.md`. Stop dependent routes that need those instructions until they exist. The embedded small-task collapse in Frame remains usable without the Autonomous run document. Never install missing companions implicitly.\\n\\n**You own the program, never the code. Author briefs, drain the queue, keep the frontier green, decide.** For a whole project handed to one standing coordinator chat: multi-day, many stacked PRs, dozens to hundreds of subagents, the human checking in twice a day instead of every five minutes. One task driven to a predicate is Autonomous run. One ambitious run needing a bespoke workflow is figure-it-out. Route here when the work outlives any single agent. Work one agent could finish inside the session's budget is not a program.\\n\\nCeremony must scale with the program. On cheap near-identical units, collapse it as each section directs.\\n\\nThe following rules govern the program.\\n\\n- Completions are queue events, not interrupts.\\n- Every spawn and every resume carries the standing orders verbatim.\\n- The brief is the product. A vague brief fails quietly, because a worker cannot ask you a question.\\n\\n#### Roles and placement\\n\\n- **Coordinator (this chat).** Local. Frames, authors briefs, drains the inbox, owns the human report, makes judgment calls. It never authors or edits code. Conflicted merges, restacks, and code changes are always tasks. Mechanically landing a verified unit (fast-forward or clean cherry-pick of a worker's commit, then push) is bookkeeping the coordinator may do itself on repos where local git is cheap. Queueing finished work behind an idle stacker is how a deadline harvests nothing. Bind spawn, follow-up, wait, result inspection and stop to exposed authorized operations. State reads and writes go through the bookkeeping helper at drain points. Most compact outputs are bounded summaries; inbox drain returns all pointers, status returns three lines, and `--json` returns complete rows. The CLI never spawns, waits, or wakes anything.\\n- **Sub-coordinator.** Always local, durable, one per track, and only when the program exceeds what one coordinator's drains can manage. A track the coordinator can drain itself needs no middle layer. Each nested layer re-pays a full orientation preamble, and a blocking sub-coordinator hides its children while the parent idles. Owns its track's units and boards, authors its workers' briefs, spawns its own workers and verifiers only when nesting and isolation are exposed and observed. Depth 3 is the desired ceiling, not a portable runtime guarantee. Rolls up aggregates at wave boundaries. Never forwards raw child reports. Cap in-flight children at what one drain can process, roughly ten, as a rolling window. Never as blocking batches, which cost the slowest child of every batch.\\n- **Worker / verifier.** Prefer remote workers when exposed and authorized. Local-only verification, this run's accessible transcripts, simulators, local IDE state and local auth require a suitable local binding. Discover control-ui and control-cli companions rather than assuming them. Remote workers cannot be assumed to read the local store, so inline required context or use paths confirmed readable by that worker. Prefer fewer, broader workers. One writer per worktree or branch (principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state). Prefer a verifier on a different observed model family. Inherit the parent selection unless explicit supported selection is observed. Unknown actual models leave diversity unverified; an unavailable required family blocks that gate.\\n\\nDepth stays at coordinator, track, worker. Author the track decomposition per project (build, landing, and verification are common cuts, not a required shape). Hard-coded swarm trees were tried and parked as too rigid.\\n\\n#### Store layout\\n\\nChoose an explicitly authorized task-owned writable `orchestrate/<project-slug>/` outside the package tree. Every file has exactly one writer. Owners publish facts, readers aggregate at read time. Use `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/orch/orch.ts --store <owned-store>`, written below as `orch`. `ORCH_STORE` is the alternative explicit binding. Plain TSV and JSON stay readable without the CLI.\\n\\n- `preferences.md` is the standing-orders register: numbered lines, one constraint each (model policy, stack shape and count, verification bar, forbidden paths, escalation policy). Paste it verbatim into every spawn and every resume. Directives decay across resumes, and each dropped one costs a human turn. When you catch yourself restating an instruction, append the line before you act (principle-encode-lessons-in-structure).\\n- `overview.md` is the durable PR and issue DB. Append. Never rewrite wholesale per event.\\n- `units.tsv` has one row per unit: id, track, state, branch, PR, head SHA, brief path. Update rows in place.\\n- `frontier.json` is the computed merge frontier, per Stack safety.\\n- `ledger.tsv` is the verification ledger, per Verification.\\n- `inbox/` holds completion pointers. `gates.md` parks human gates (question, options, default on no answer).\\n- `decisions.tsv` is the trail via the show-me-your-work skill.\\n- `status.md` is derived from `units.tsv` and `ledger.tsv` at each drain, never hand-maintained. Regenerate it from the tables instead of narrating events into it.\\n\\n\\n#### Helper contract\\n\\nRead [orch CLI](../scripts/orch/orch.ts), [store](../scripts/orch/store.ts), [tests](../scripts/orch/orch.test.ts), [bootstrap](../scripts/bootstrap.ts), [manifest](../scripts/package.json) and [lock](../scripts/bun.lock). The CLI requires the exact pinned dependencies in a separately authorized writable copy. The operative package has no installed dependencies; the tested helper snapshot is evidence for that snapshot only. No automatic install occurs. Read docs/testing/helper-setup.md for the exact-copy validation boundary and retained historical setup evidence. It grants no installation approval and transfers no historical pass to this caller. Any future setup needs fresh explicit authorization for the exact writable copy, registry, disabled lifecycle scripts and task-owned cache under Herd. Missing dependencies block execution.\\n\\nUse these actual commands through the explicit `orch` binding:\\n\\n- `init`; `standing add <line>`; `standing show --json`. Compact standing output truncates after four rows, so use JSON or read preferences.md to obtain every standing order.\\n- `unit add <id> --track <track> --brief <path>`; `unit set <id> --state <state> --branch <branch> --pr <number> --sha <full-head-sha>`; `unit get <id>`; `unit list --json`.\\n- `ledger record <pr> <full-head-sha> <verdict> --evidence <path> --verifier <identity>`; `ledger check <pr> <full-head-sha>`; `ledger summary`. A missing exact key returns NOT-VERIFIED and exit 2. Usage or runtime failure returns exit 1; success returns 0.\\n- `inbox push <agent> <unit> <status> --report <path>`; `inbox drain --peek --json`; `inbox drain --json`; `inbox count`. Peek before drain, persist that receipt to an owned artifact and read it back. Capture the complete actual drain output to another owned receipt and verify readback before classifying pointers. Drain removes the queued pointers; arrivals between peek and drain can change the actual batch. If the receipt is lost or interruption makes consumption uncertain, reconcile actual artifacts before retrying or updating rows.\\n- `gate park <id> --question <question> --options <options> --default <answer>`; `gate list --json`; `gate resolve <id> --answer <answer>`. Resolve permission gates only from actual authorization.\\n- `frontier set --repo <stack-owner-clone>`, optionally `--prs <bottom-to-top-numbers>`; `frontier show --json`; `status`. Frontier discovery runs local git and gt inspection against that clone. Missing gt metadata, malformed output or pin mismatch is an error, never guessed frontier state.\\n\\nThe helper does not spawn, wait, wake, enforce worker ownership, validate full revision syntax for unit or ledger input, inspect evidence paths, enforce terminal states or verify permissions. Keep immutable assignments and append-only attempts separately under the assignment contract. Match identity, input revision, full current head SHA, artifacts and observed method before accepting results. Ledger counts include historical revisions; filter against the current unit and frontier heads before counting verified completions. A done unit string, ledger label or open-gate count proves no worker completion or authorization. Coordinator-owned bookkeeping may record worker facts; give each worker separate result and receipt paths. Atomic rename is not proof of crash durability or safe adversarial concurrent access.\\n\\n#### The brief\\n\\nYour prompts to agents are your only product, and a sloppy brief compounds into slop across the whole tree. Every spawn carries all of it.
